I have 40 years of experience, only 6 mu to manage, and I have well irrigation, so I will keep to a steady, familiar plan instead of taking risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen for strong tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus for roots, and a moderate amount of potassium to keep the crop standing well. I will irrigate several times because wheat in my area depends on timely water at key stages. I will use rotary tillage because it fits my scale and saves labor. For maize, I will plant hybrid seed after wheat because I want stable yield on limited land. I will give maize solid nitrogen, with moderate phosphorus and potassium, irrigate fewer times than wheat, and control pests only as needed. I will stay with practices I know I can manage well at my age and with a two-person household, aiming for reliable output rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
